precisionNotes.original: stronger than separately stated FORALL t AE omega
precisionNotes.reviewerClarification: For natural-number time the two forms are logically equivalent by countable intersection. AE omega forall t is syntactically stronger-looking and exposes one common event, but is not mathematically stronger here. The extractor explicitly cites countability, and its graph has the correct obligation. This review adopts the precise equivalence.

derivedObligationReview.scope: The observation map H_t(omega)=(S(omega),(Y_i(omega))_{i<t}) and its comap information sigma field; F_t lies below it. F need not be a monotone filtration.
For each t select an F_t-strongly-measurable representative equal to prediction_t almost everywhere. This is a proof ingredient, not a new public assumption.

Use/prove real-valued measurable factorization through H_t for a representative measurable with respect to the comap. Must check exact factorization theorem hypotheses; no standard-Borel or measurability assumption on S/Y is silently added to target1.

Apply measurable projection/clamping R->[0,1] to the policy on every seed-history pair. Preserve agreement where the original prediction is in [0,1]; behavior on unattained histories and null sets may change.
Intersect the countably many almost-sure agreement and boundedness events to obtain one a.e. event on which equality holds for every natural t. No uncountable-time conclusion.
From iIndepFun Y and independence of S from the entire stream, derive joint independence of (S,Y_{<t}) from Y_t. Pairwise independence alone is not a substitute.
Formulate independence of the current draw from the sigma field generated by seed and past, then restrict to F<=that sigma field.
Transport joint independence through a measurable real-valued function of the history.
Transfer independence from a measurable representative to the original ae-equal P. Target2 requires neither boundedness nor identical laws.
In target2/3, measurable S and Y make H_t ambient-measurable; F<=comap gives measurable representatives in the ambient space. Target1 alone needs no ambient measurability of S/Y.
Use probability measure and a.s. [0,1] bounds to establish integrability of predictions, observations, squares, products and finite sums. Null-set outliers do not change integrals.
Let m=integral Y_0 and v=E[(Y_0-m)^2]. Common law supplies every observation mean/variance; a.s. [0,1] support implies m in [0,1].
Expand (P-Y_t)^2=(P-m)^2+(Y_t-m)^2-2(P-m)(Y_t-m), use independence and integrability to factor the product expectation and make it zero.
For each u in [0,1], expected cumulative fixed loss=T*(v+(u-m)^2). The image is nonempty and bounded below, with minimum Tv attained at m; its sInf is therefore Tv.
Interchange integral and finite sum after integrability; subtract Tv to derive expectedFixedRegret=sum_t E[(prediction_t-m)^2].
Each squared-error integral is nonnegative, so the finite sum and expectedFixedRegret are nonnegative.
At T=0 all sums vanish and the expected-fixed-loss image is {0}; sInf and regret are0. The source uses positive game horizons; this is the sealed target natural-number extension.

An alternative derived proof can first construct the target1 bounded explicit policy and then prove its squared-risk identity, transporting the finite losses back via common a.e. equality. This is optional, not required by the direct representative route.

antiAnchoringChecks.argument: Independent fair bits Y0,Y1 and seed S=Y0 xor Y1: S is independent of each bit separately, yet (S,Y0) reveals Y1. Thus whole-stream independence cannot be dropped.

antiAnchoringChecks.test: same law without independence is insufficient
antiAnchoringChecks.argument: Let every Y_t be the same fair bit and predict Y_{t-1} for t>0. Past reveals current, so the variance lower bound fails. Common law alone cannot justify T2/T3.
At T=1 with a fair Bernoulli outcome, min_u E[(u-Y)^2]=1/4 but E[min_u (u-Y)^2]=0.
For Y_t=0 and prediction_t=1, all admissibility conditions hold with constant seed, while excess=T. T3 cannot imply little-o or zero average error.
A predictor equal to an admissible constant except on a null singleton can take value 2 there. T1 conclusion is AE equality and bounded policy, not pointwise preservation of original values.

antiAnchoringChecks.test: bounded T1 cannot close unbounded T2
antiAnchoringChecks.argument: T2 permits every real AE-measurable P without hpb. An unbounded measurable function of seed is admitted; invoking T1 needs a separate justified transform or an unbounded factorization lemma, not assumption insertion.
